scenario: [LGRA.13.3] with [LUNI.8.5] and [LCST.4.5.2]: a rule reads a `const` whose value is a `::` cast of another `const`. `RAW = WARM::Float` strips the unit from `WARM = 21.5_celsius`, which is its stored base-unit number, 294.65 K ([LUNI.8.5]); `TEXT = N::String` converts the `Int` `const N = 42` to `"42"` ([LCST.4.5.2]). A `Reading` carrying those two values makes both rules fire. Pin: `raw`, then `text`. A compiler that gives a `const` name no static type cannot type either cast's operand, so it leaves both rules unlowered and the program is refused. PATH PINNED: `dsc.typecheck.lgra_13_3_const_type`, which types a `const` name from its right-hand side, and `dsc.rete`'s `ex_cast` arm, which then finds the cast's pair (`lcst_4_cast_pair`), against each runtime's evaluation of the strip (an identity) and of `FN_INT_TO_STRING`.
rules_ds:
unit celsius: temperature = x + 273.15

const WARM = 21.5_celsius
const RAW = WARM::Float
const N = 42
const TEXT = N::String

schema Reading scope logical:
    id: String key
    f: Float mutable
    s: String mutable

rule raw:
    Reading r where r.f == RAW
->
    log info "raw"

rule text:
    Reading r where r.s == TEXT
->
    log info "text"
